hero.h1: The incident board for the command post.
hero.lede: KP Rück turns the magnetic board in the rear command post into a digital one: incidents, crews, vehicles and equipment on one board – live on every device.
hero.ctaNote: No account – pick a role and go
hero.frameAlt: Incident board: columns from received through to closed, incident cards in between, crews on the left, equipment on the right

fit.note: Grown out of the real operational work of Feuerwehr Oberwil BL – proven there, and developed further ever since.

own.p: KP Rück is open source and runs on a machine in your own station or in your own cloud. Incidents, crews, vehicles and equipment stay under your control.
items: No licence fees
No vendor lock-in
Run it yourself, extend it yourself

tenet.quote: «When the network is gone, paper is in charge»
tenet.expl: A board that goes black in a power cut is not a command tool. So redundancy is built in at several levels – every level works without the one above it.

stages.h3: Several devices on the same state
stages.p: Tablets, projector displays and phones all hang live off the same board. If one device fails or freezes, another carries on – there is nothing to rescue and nothing to catch up on.

stages.h3: A second instance at the station
stages.p: KP Rück can also be run locally alongside. The built-in sync keeps events, incidents, crews, vehicles, equipment and settings in step between the cloud and the local database. The map comes from your own tile server, and the printer is on the LAN anyway.

The state of the board goes to the thermal printer every few minutes, the situation sheet at the push of a button. If everything fails, the last sheet becomes the board. On restart, one person transfers what was done by hand back into the app.

incident.eyebrow: From the alarm to the report
incident.lede: This is what a storm night looks like in the command post – what happens on the board ends up in the incident report afterwards.

entries.p: Through the reporting form, by telephone, or over the open interface from the dispatch system (Divera, for example). The duty officer takes one over with a click – the report becomes an incident on the board.

Personnel, vehicles and equipment onto the incident by drag and drop. The system helps the incident commander spot and surface double bookings, missing resources and contradictions. Whoever arrives checks themselves in with a QR code.
Every incident on one map, with the vehicles optionally by GPS position. When a vehicle reaches the scene, the board proposes the status change itself.
The recon team fills in the form on their own phone – photos included. The report hangs on the right incident instead of getting lost in a group chat.
The projector in the command post, the tablet on the table and the quartermaster's phone all show the same state – without anybody pressing «refresh».

entries.h3: The incident report writes itself along the way.
entries.p: The incident log and the response times build up as you go and turn into a PDF. Corrections are made with new entries, not with an eraser – so the night stays on the record.

shots.lede: Every image is taken from the public demo. Click «Open the demo» and you are standing at the same board.

features.lede: Grown out of real events and exercises, not out of a feature list. Everything that comes from outside – alerting, GPS, printers – is optional: KP Rück also runs entirely without those connections.

sibling.h2: KP Rück keeps the overview at the rear. KP Front commands at the front.
sibling.p: KP Front turns the situation map and the command table at the scene into digital ones: tactical symbols, site plans and SCBA monitoring, even without a network. Its own app, the same handwriting – the two can hand alarms to each other, but neither needs the other.
sibling.cta: Take a look at KP Front

items.a: No more double bookings. No report lost in a group chat. Less radio traffic for questions that are on the board anyway. Everybody sees the same picture at the same time – and the incident report is already there when you get back, instead of the weekend after.
You do. Every fire brigade runs its own KP Rück – on its own machine at the station or in the cloud. You decide where incident data, crew and fleet live; nothing goes to a vendor or to third parties.
Nothing. KP Rück is open source (AGPL) – no licence, no subscription, no per-device fee. What remains is your own running costs: a small server, or a machine at the station.

items.q: What does it take to run?
items.a: Less than most people assume. A small mini-PC or server at the station is enough, and setting it up takes a few hours. After that the system largely runs by itself, and updates are one command. You need somebody to set it up once – in the brigade, at the municipality, or a friendly IT contact. And if you have nobody: get in touch, we will help with the setup.

items.q: Can we adapt it to how we work?
items.a: Yes. Every brigade has its own administration area: incident types, priorities, crew, fleet and equipment lists are all configurable there, and import and export run through Excel. And because the whole code is on GitHub , everything else can be built – by you or to order.
With the demo, without an account – pick a role and go. Then try it on an exercise; exercise mode is cleanly separated from the real thing. And if it fits: get in touch, we will help with the setup.

contact.p: Do you want to try KP Rück at your brigade? Is something missing, or does something not work the way you expect? Get in touch – we read everything.
contact.alt: For questions and open-ended ideas there are the GitHub discussions.

footer.origin: Born out of the operational work of Feuerwehr Oberwil BL – because on incidents we kept seeing the same sources of error: double bookings, scattered information and transcription mistakes made by hand. Every fire brigade runs its own KP Rück, with its own crew, its own vehicles and its own data.
